correctness_confidence.basis: All algebraic lemmas are rigorously verified via an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 module (0 sorry, 0 warnings) and tested across 16 exact straight-line DAG certificates in Python with arbitrary-precision integers and fractions.

novelty.basis: Pioneers the reconciliation of sub-logarithmic N(log N)^{1/2} FFT bounds with scalar bit-width blow-up over C versus fixed-width bounded-exponent NTTs over post-quantum finite fields like Kyber.

reproducibility.basis: Complete reproducibility via standalone Lean 4 ledger and pure-stdlib Python verifier scripts that independently execute 16 certified instances and 50 adversarial red-team tests.

rigor.basis: Exhaustive algebraic proofs connect Morgenstern volume bounds, determinant orthogonality, Pythagorean brackets, and finite-field NTT precision requirements with zero reliance on floating-point approximations.

significance.basis: Resolves fundamental architectural trade-offs between complex arithmetic dynamic range and finite-field exactness, providing actionable insights for post-quantum lattice cryptography implementations.

strengths: Rigorous 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 formalization (0 sorry, 0 warnings).
Clear identification of the precision dichotomy between complex FFTs requiring super-polynomial scalar weight blow-up and finite-field NTTs escaping Archimedean constraints.
Exact rational bracketing of Pythagorean rectangular rank-support separation.
Comprehensive straight-line DAG verifier (FOURIER-GATE-CERT-1.0) with robust adversarial red-team testing.
strong_novelty_candidates: Morgenstern Gate-Bit Conservation Law applied to sub-logarithmic FFTs
Complex-FFT vs. Bounded-Exponent Finite-Field NTT Precision Dichotomy
Zero-float straight-line DAG certification framework with 18-theorem Lean 4 backing
summary: This paper establishes the precise trade-offs between sub-logarithmic complex FFT bounds and scalar weight/bit-width blow-up via Morgenstern Gate-Bit Conservation, distinguishes complex FFTs from bounded-exponent finite-field NTTs (such as ML-KEM/Kyber), proves exact Pythagorean rank-support rational brackets, and provides a 0-sorry Lean 4 formalization alongside 16 certified straight-line DAG instances verified with zero floating-point arithmetic.
weaknesses: Verification is currently demonstrated up to N <= 16 due to full N-basis simulation constraints in Python verifier, leaving larger N sub-logarithmic circuits to randomized algebraic checks.
Concrete constant c0 for product-group NTTs over F_3329 and F_8380417 remains an open engineering estimation challenge.
